mechanism_fit: This realises HA (M10, with M3 and M2 tags). The entry point E is EarthMoversDistance.compute(double[], double[]), an existing public method with a small, self-contained computation: the 1-D earth mover's distance between two histograms on unit-spaced bins. A context edit turns E's body into the single statement `return EnumeratedDistribution.transportCost(a, b);`. H1 is EnumeratedDistribution.transportCost (package distribution). It composes H2 = Frequency.occupiedBins (package stat), which lists the bins non-empty in either histogram, and H3 = Sum.carriedCost (package stat.descriptive.summary), which carries the running surplus from one occupied bin to the next and charges |surplus| times the number of unit steps travelled. The chain spans 4 classes in 4 packages, and every helper is a new public static method in an existing production class. The gold is the deep helper H3. Its fault is a quiet omission of a step its javadoc promises: it adds |surplus| once per occupied bin and drops the distance factor (next - j). The remaining loop reads as a complete 'sum of |surplus| over the occupied bins'. It is invisible whenever no bin that is empty in both histograms is crossed by a nonzero surplus. That holds for every existing test, which uses dense histograms. The trigger calls E directly on two six-bin histograms with gaps and fails on E's return value (1.0 instead of the textbook EMD 2.0).
gold: org.apache.commons.math3.stat.descriptive.summary.Sum::carriedCost (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/stat/descriptive/summary/Sum.java). The fault removes the line `final int next = k + 1 < bins.length ? bins[k + 1] : a.length;` and changes `cost += FastMath.abs(surplus) * (next - j);` to `cost += FastMath.abs(surplus);`. The minimal repair restores those two lines in carriedCost.
decoys: org.apache.commons.math3.ml.distance.EarthMoversDistance::compute (E, entry point): after the context edit its body is one delegation to H1, and its javadoc says it returns transportCost's value
org.apache.commons.math3.distribution.EnumeratedDistribution::transportCost (H1): returns exactly Sum.carriedCost(a, b, Frequency.occupiedBins(a, b)), as its javadoc states

org.apache.commons.math3.stat.Frequency::occupiedBins (H2): returns the increasing indices i < a.length with a[i] != 0 or b[i] != 0, as documented; pinned by the new FrequencyTest.testNonEmptyPositions
ownership_reason: EarthMoversDistance.compute (E) is one delegation to EnumeratedDistribution.transportCost (H1), whose javadoc says it returns exactly Sum.carriedCost(a, b, Frequency.occupiedBins(a, b)), and that is its whole body. Frequency.occupiedBins (H2) is documented to return, in increasing order, exactly the indices i < a.length with a[i] != 0 or b[i] != 0, leaving out bins that are empty in both histograms. On the trigger histograms {0.5,0,0,0.5,0,0} and {0,0,0.5,0,0,0.5} it returns {0,2,3,5}, as documented; the new FrequencyTest.testNonEmptyPositions passes on the variant and pins this contract. Sum.carriedCost (H3, the gold) is documented to visit the listed bins with a running surplus (a[j] + surplus) - b[j], to carry that surplus from bin j to the next listed bin (or to a.length after the last one), and to charge |surplus| * (next - j), because unlisted bins are empty and are only crossed. Its code adds |surplus| once per listed bin and drops the factor (next - j). The two half-unit surpluses each travel two unit steps (bin 0 to 2 and bin 3 to 5), so each is charged 0.5 instead of 1.0. The trigger therefore gets 1.0 instead of 2.0, and 2.0 is the textbook earth mover's distance for these histograms (0.5 moved two bins, twice). The existing EarthMoversDistanceTest cases (test, testZero, testZero2) pass on the variant: their histograms have no bin that is empty in both while a surplus crosses it, so every gap is one step. They pin the E/H1/H2/H3 composition on dense input. E and H1 do exactly what their javadoc says (delegate or compose) and promise nothing about distance weighting. Restoring the (next - j) factor and its next line in carriedCost alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass. Making occupiedBins list every bin would also make the trigger pass, but it contradicts occupiedBins' documented contract and fails FrequencyTest.testNonEmptyPositions (declared G9 edit). Swapping the argument order in E or H1, or keying occupancy on one histogram, does not make the trigger pass. Ownership tests: FrequencyTest::testNonEmptyPositions (new) and EarthMoversDistanceTest::test (existing); both pass on the CORRECT and the variant configuration.
trigger: org.apache.commons.math3.ml.distance.EarthMoversDistanceTest::testSixBinHistograms, a new JUnit4 method in src/test/java/org/apache/commons/math3/ml/distance/EarthMoversDistanceTest.java. It asserts assertEquals(2.0, new EarthMoversDistance().compute({0.5,0,0,0.5,0,0}, {0,0,0.5,0,0,0.5}), 1e-12). All values are exact binary fractions, so the result is deterministic. Extra test: FrequencyTest::testNonEmptyPositions (ownership test for H2).
construction_notes: Most of the effort went into finding a quiet location in Math. The S1-style candidates (ChiSquareTest/GTest rescaling, Pearson correlation, Canberra, KS, Halton, Quaternion polar form, distributions) all had a correct sibling, a USED host class, or existing tests that exercise every natural omission. EarthMoversDistance has a single dense test pair, and no bin in it is empty in both histograms, so a sparse (occupied-bin) decomposition places the distance weighting in a helper whose omission only shows when a surplus crosses an empty gap. That is a natural, balanced trigger whose expected value is the textbook EMD. An earlier idea, an exclusive prefix scan of the surplus, was dropped. It is only visible for histograms of unequal total mass, which is outside EMD's usual domain, and H1 could absorb it by adding |sum(a) - sum(b)|. Hand checks on a /private/tmp copy: the CORRECT configuration passes the full suite (4380 tests, 0 failures, plus trigger and ownership tests); the variant fails only the trigger with 'expected:<2.0> but was:<1.0>'. Each declared compensating edit was also checked: listing every bin in occupiedBins makes the trigger pass but fails FrequencyTest.testNonEmptyPositions; keying occupancy on a only gives 1.5; swapping the argument order in H1 or E gives 1.0. The validator ran once. Scratch copies were deleted, and the pristine checkout was not modified. Validator: overall READY on the first attempt (all gates G0-G13 pass). Packaged as CTV-9EB2B7.
concerns: 1) Behaviour preservation is bitwise for every existing test, but only up to rounding in general. The CORRECT carriedCost charges |surplus| * gap once, where the pristine loop adds |surplus| once per crossed bin, so histograms with interior or trailing doubly-empty bins can differ in the last ulp. 2) A full behavioural repair exists at H2: one line makes occupiedBins list every bin, after which the unit charge per listed bin covers the gaps. It contradicts occupiedBins' javadoc and fails the new ownership test, so G9 rejects it. An auditor could still argue that skipping empty bins is an artificial design choice that creates the dependency. Similarly, H1 could pass an all-indices array instead of occupiedBins(a, b). That is not a natural one-liner in Java 5, it contradicts H1's javadoc, and it was not declared. 3) E's class-level javadoc ('Earth Mover's distance') states the overall semantics that the variant violates. This is inherent to HA. E's own method javadoc ({@inheritDoc} plus 'the value returned is the one computed by transportCost') is satisfied by its one-line body. 4) The gold edit spans two adjacent lines: it deletes the `next` local and drops `* (next - j)`. After the fault, the loop index k is used only for bins[k], a faint hint that something was removed. 5) The helper host classes (EnumeratedDistribution, Frequency, Sum) are loose semantic homes for histogram-transport helpers, and EarthMoversDistance gains a dependency on the distribution package. Sum also has an unrelated weighted-sum evaluate(values, weights). 6) No test can pin H1 on sparse input independently of the gold. The existing EMD tests pin the composition only on dense histograms. 7) The expected value 2.0 can be checked from first principles (0.5 moved two bins, twice), so the trigger itself is unambiguous. A model can easily localise the omission once it reads carriedCost's javadoc. The instance tests ranking (E vs H3), not search.
